content:
We have carbon NMR data: chemical shifts: 166.40, 131.87, 129.70 (twice), 129.01 (twice), 129.00, 52.24, 43.47, 38.60.

We need number of CH3 groups (methyl). Need to infer structure. Carbon shifts: 166.40 likely carbonyl (C=O). Aromatic carbons around 129-132 (multiple). 52.24, 43.47, 38.60 likely aliphatic carbons. Methyl carbons typically around 10-30 ppm for simple alkyl, but 38-52 could be attached to heteroatoms or aromatic. Could be e.g., acetyl group (CH3CO) carbonyl at 166, methyl carbon at ~30. But we have 166 carbonyl, but no ~30 shift; we have 52, 43, 38. Maybe the methyl is attached to heteroatom (O-CH3 ~55 ppm). 52.24 could be OCH3. 43.47 maybe CH2 attached to carbonyl? 38.60 maybe CH2.

Thus likely one methyl (OCH3). Could there be more? No low-field methyl signals. So answer likely 1.

But verify with proton NMR? Could request proton NMR to see methyl signals. Let's get proton NMR.
